OLV Pulhof, Berchem: School refused to pay a ransom, then attackers tried to extort parents directly.
AZ Monica, Antwerp/Deurne: Ransomware. All servers off, about 50% capacity, 7 patients transferred. Paper for about 3 weeks. No patient data leak found.
The city administration of Heinsberg could not be reached by phone or email for days after a cyberattack.
A small company's server was fully encrypted by ransomware (HardBit); it restored everything from its regular backups.
a pro-Russian group (NoName057(16)) aimed 74.6% of all its attacks that week at Czechia: 3,803 attacks on government services, vital infrastructure and media (SOCRadar).
The Nova group claimed KPMG Netherlands.
the state IT provider Valtori was breached through its phone-management software: details of about 20,000 government devices and users. Police treat it as suspected espionage.
Cyprus was named among the countries probably reached by an Asian espionage group that broke into sensitive systems in more than 37 countries. The government denies any breach of its systems.
the Estonian Olympic Committee's website was attacked; NoName057(16) claimed it.
an attack claimed by pro-Russian activists paralysed Deutsche Bahn's booking systems, app and departure boards for hours.

around the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics, Italy blocked attacks on about 120 Foreign Ministry sites and on hotels in Cortina. The government called them Russian in origin; NoName057(16) claimed them. La Sapienza University in Rome was hit in the same days.
telecom operator Odido: data of about 6.2 million customer accounts, including identity-document and bank-account numbers.
phone-management flaws exploited at the Data Protection Authority and the Council for the Judiciary.
FortiBleed: 270+ Belgian organisations: Fortinet firewalls compromised. Attackers still had admin rights on 100+ Belgian firewalls in June. None of those examined had MFA.
Norway's security service disclosed that the Chinese state-linked group Salt Typhoon had exploited vulnerable network devices in Norway.
The Medusa group claimed the municipality of Battipaglia.
BDH-Klinik Greifswald: the communication network was paralysed and theft of patient data was later confirmed.
The municipality of Chioggia and its services company reported a cyberattack on the company's digital systems, with possible effects on some services.
The trade union CFDT confirmed that members' personal data was taken.
The Qilin group listed the University of Mannheim as a victim.
The agricultural company UBM Group reported a ransomware attack.
The prison service reported a data leak through the hack of its phone-management software.
the Digital Security Authority told parliament that attacks had become daily and that some state departments had received ransom demands.
An outsider reached a list of laptops managed by the state IT centre, with users' names, phone numbers and work email addresses. The government says no citizens' data was touched.
The regional hospital in Szczecin: ransomware forced staff to work on paper; the attackers reportedly demanded several million dollars.
The defence ministry confirmed 67 cyberattacks on the Romanian Air Force, with a few dozen email accounts compromised.
A management application of the Catholic school network: data of about 1.5 million pupils, families and teachers exposed.
the Malta Gaming Authority confirmed a breach of one of its systems. A German security researcher said she had reached compliance files and player records.
Ikea Norway: data on up to 42,370 customers and 3,261 employees downloaded through a flaw at a group IT supplier.
Nandrin (municipality): LockBit 5.0 claimed it and published data on the dark web.
The Eskulap medical centre in Racibórz: medical records encrypted, with a high risk that data was stolen.
the health-recruitment platform Healthdaq detected unauthorised access; the XP95 group claims 431 GB, including CVs and identity documents.
A rehabilitation centre in the Świętokrzyskie region: ransomware encrypted data and cut access to systems.
a cyber incident disrupted access to state online services, including the e-government portal. Officials said internal systems were not breached.
ransomware at Kurita Europe, an industrial water-treatment firm in Mannheim.
a Russian-linked email-spying campaign (at least 284 mailboxes, Sept 2024–Mar 2026) reached Greek military targets.
researchers (Bellingcat) found Hungarian government email addresses with passwords in 795 leaked data sets, including passwords like "Password".
ChipSoft ransomware, a supplier to about 70% of Dutch hospitals.

ChipSoft (Dutch hospital-software supplier): Ransomware. Dutch hospitals closed patient portals. Early reports spoke of Belgian impact; on 16 April ChipSoft said no Belgian care institution was hit. Data was stolen at a few Dutch institutions and later said to be destroyed. The group behind it is not confirmed.
Anderlues (municipality): Night-time attack. Administrative services closed indefinitely. TheGentlemen ransomware listed it on 19 Apr.
ransomware at the municipalities of Vilhelmina and Dorotea.
the national agency for identity documents (ANTS) was breached; it confirmed 11.7 million accounts. A 15-year-old was charged.
Lørenskog municipality: a large amount of data stolen and offered for sale on the dark web.
Medical-device maker Medtronic, headquartered in Dublin: health information of 3.8 million people reportedly stolen worldwide; the company attributes it to the ShinyHunters group.
Cosmetics chain Rituals confirmed that customers' personal data was taken.
cabinetmedical.be: Data leak.
Vanden Borre: A threat actor offered 264,000 records for sale.
VUB, Thomas More, Artevelde, KdG, Erasmushogeschool, CVO Gent: Canvas learning-platform breach (ShinyHunters). Names, emails and student numbers of thousands of people.
Christeyns: Cyberattack.
Schools in Styria: a ransomware group (Payload) claimed 21 GB of data; the education authority refused to negotiate and the outage was fixed quickly.

The ShinyHunters group named Icelandic schools, among them the University of Iceland and Reykjavik University, as victims of its attack on the learning platform Canvas; no leak of Icelandic data is confirmed.
A billing service provider for hospitals: data of more than 100,000 private patients of German university hospitals taken.
Health-insurance payment operator Almerys confirmed a breach covering 15.4 million social security numbers.
Ransomware at a hospital group (not named): operations postponed and emergency rooms sent patients elsewhere.
about 62,000 records with personal data of doctors leaked from an agency of the Ministry of Health.
the Qilin ransomware group claimed the business-jet operator Avcon Jet. 23 Jul 2026: the group TheGentlemen claimed the fertility clinic Wunschkind Klinik Dr Brunbauer.
the ransomware group TheGentlemen claimed the Ministry of Health and threatened to publish data.
The Ministry of Health said an attack hit some of its applications, while the system holding patients' medical data was not affected.

The state forest company Latvijas valsts meži: a foreign ransomware group leaked 44 GB of data. The national cyber team had flagged the weakness two years earlier and it was never fixed. A pharmaceutical maker's server was reportedly compromised by the same attacker.
the tax authority was breached; data on about 678,000 taxpayers was stolen. The ministry confirmed it after the data was offered on a criminal forum.
the financial group Eurohold and its insurer Euroins said they stopped an attack; the Krybit group listed both on its leak site.
the public transport operator Metro Mondego confirmed a ransomware attack (claimed by The Gentlemen); personal data of pass holders was probably copied.
Chaumont hospital: cyberattack with loss of data and critical systems unavailable.
Ransomware attacks on healthcare bodies (7 and 13 July, Qilin group) and on municipal offices (16 July, The Gentlemen group); victims not named.

ransomware at the national land registry agency ANCPI. The servers running its applications were encrypted and deleted, and the property market came to a standstill because no sale could be registered. The hacker says he wiped the land registry database after his blackmail failed; the agency says its central database was not compromised and that it holds an offline copy. Romania's cyber directorate said the attack was not complex and used weaknesses the agency had been told to fix. Services were still limited in August.
The Play group claimed the business-services firm Tax MT.
The primary-care network PaKK-MED disclosed a ransomware attack with a potential data leak.
Ministries acknowledged serious incidents after the EU named Slovakia among the targets of Russia's FSB; the targets were vital infrastructure, the energy sector and the arms industry.
A ransomware group published about 222 GB taken from a fiduciary firm in the canton of Vaud, including data on municipalities and a member of the cantonal government.
The federal IT office detected an intrusion on its SharePoint servers; about 200 accounts were compromised. Officials say no sensitive data was accessed.

Attackers copied data on about 31,000 legal entities from the national register of the real owners of companies and foundations. The government set up a crisis unit; the register was taken offline for outside users.
ransomware in the Berlin state network after one click on a fake link; the Rhysida group demanded 30 bitcoin (about €2 million). The Berlin Senate refused to pay.
hackers stole files from the State Legal Council, the state's own lawyers, and demanded hundreds of thousands of euros in cryptocurrency. It did not pay (To Vima).
ransomware at the Municipality of Sithonia and its port fund, which share IT systems.

the State Treasury confirmed an attack on the network of its agricultural payments division; files on staff computers were encrypted. Officials say no customer data was lost; first findings pointed to Russian servers.
The Chamber of Employees reported unauthorised access to some of its servers; personal data may have been taken.

Hvidovre Hospital: ransomware on the network that runs the building's technical systems was stopped; access-card data of about 7,600 staff, including personal ID numbers, may have been taken. Patient care was not affected.
E-scooter company Ryde: unauthorised access exposed 4.5 million accounts, 1.6 million of them in Norway.
ransomware at EOPPEP, the national body that certifies qualifications (official announcement).
An attack on logistics company Ceva Logistics led to data leaks at at least twelve companies in the Netherlands.
the road traffic safety agency CSDD, which keeps the vehicle register, was breached; a data leak affecting about 1.2 million people, two-thirds of the population.
Université libre de Bruxelles: Qilin ransomware claim. Employee login credentials found exposed.
A Russian hacker group claimed an attack that disrupted government digital services.
An attack hit the mobile app of the pension institute; the institute said its core system and pension payments were not affected.
Patient and staff data of a Czech healthcare body were offered for sale by attackers.
Iceland's cyber team warned that Icelandic websites had been compromised to push malware onto visitors through fake verification prompts.

intruders read about 8.8 million records of the national population register (CPR): names, addresses and personal ID numbers, including people who have died or emigrated. They did not break into the register itself; they used the legitimate access of a private IT company. The hacker claims one account had the password "123456"; that claim is not verified.
physical sabotage of electricity substations in Brandenburg and Bergheim; drone attack on Leipzig airport, blamed on Russia.
the payment app Revolut disclosed customer information after fake requests sent from a real government email domain; a hacker claimed about 680 accounts, Maltese ones among them.
an attack took the IT of six casinos of the Hit group offline.
Jims (fitness chain): Data theft.
The INC Ransom group listed the Policlinico Triestino hospital; the hospital has not confirmed it.
The national cyber institute warned of a ransomware campaign against Hungarian companies using fake emails in the name of the Prosecutor's Office.

the City of Vienna learned from the national cyber team that about 26,000 internal documents had been copied, with data on roughly 6,000 people. The weakness had reportedly been offered for sale on an online forum beforehand. No ransom demand.
Machelen (municipality): Digital services down after a phishing attack (mayor to VRT). No sign of data leaking.
The LockBit group claimed the municipality of Robecco sul Naviglio.
Ransomware groups claimed the hydrogen-equipment maker HyGear (LockBit) and the cold-storage firm Blokland Cold Stores (Gunra).
Hôpital Paris Saint-Joseph confirmed a leak covering 15,044 patients.
A compromise was detected in the civil service and remote access for parts of it was shut down temporarily (one source; not corroborated).
Charité Berlin, contact details of about 140,000 people; attacks on public hospitals on 8 Oct.
police said an 18-year-old in Athens is suspected of writing ransomware for the KillSec group; three arrests in an international operation.
Ahold Delhaize outage (Albert Heijn, Etos, Gall & Gall). Nov 2026: refrigeration incidents. About 300 Dutch firewalls in FortiBleed.
ransomware took all IT systems of one municipality down.
Building-materials supplier DPL Group listed as a ransomware victim.
the Ministry of Agriculture shut down its computers; online services went down.

The health service of Extremadura detected a breach of its online health-centre app on 5 October: clinical information of 18,416 users was compromised. Police arrested the suspected attacker on 29 October.

A software supplier of the federal pension fund Publica reported a cyberattack; data on more than 100,000 insured people may have been taken. The Akira group was named in press reports; not confirmed.
An attack on an IT company that worked for the intelligence services let hackers obtain unclassified data of the services and other bodies; the intelligence system confirmed it.
about 700 supermarket sites (Intermarché, Coopérative U), Danfoss and Copeland/Dixell controllers, 15+ fires. Attributed by France to Iran's Revolutionary Guards unit Shahid Kaveh on 9 Nov.
Ahold Delhaize (group): Systems taken offline group-wide. Mainly Dutch and US web services hit. Its second major incident in two years.
Booking data leaked at tourism bodies in Tyrol, Styria and Salzburg, including 97 hotels in Salzburg, through stolen interface logins.
suspected ransomware at a radio-communications operator.
a test environment of the University of Copenhagen was breached; about 525,000 people, including national ID numbers.
State agencies took their websites offline as a precaution over two critical flaws in widely used web software.
FPS Finance (MyMinfin, Tax-on-web, Biztax): Intrusion contained within hours, services taken offline. No data taken per the FPS. Filing deadline moved to 16 Nov.
A login flaw in the school system Inna, used by up to 16 upper-secondary schools, let a student try to change other pupils' grades and attendance.
AVOCATS.BE: Order-management software breached. About 27,500 non-lawyer contacts. No banking or sensitive data, per the organisation.
After the breach of the state administration system, the land survey authority shut down part of its online services "for security reasons".
refrigeration incidents reported in the freezer wave.
refrigeration incidents reported in the freezer wave.
a Russian state-linked spy group (Turla) was reported to have compromised government email servers to read messages involving NATO and the EU.
an intruder reached a state web server and took more than 15,000 user records of the state administration's internal system; officials had to change their passwords.

Delhaize, Carrefour, Spar (Colruyt), Intermarché, IKEA Mons: Freezer controllers hijacked and temperatures raised; food thrown away. Carrefour 15/700 stores, Spar 5, Delhaize dozens (about 40 in BE+LU). Federal prosecutor investigating.
a freezer at a Selver supermarket was set to 50 °C in the refrigeration wave.
refrigeration manipulated in North Rhine-Westphalia and at an Edeka store in Reisbach (confirmed by the federal cyber office BSI).
refrigeration systems at 13 of 223 SuperValu stores (Musgrave Group) were affected in the freezer wave.
Delhaize stores hit in the freezer wave.
23+ ICA and 7 Coop stores, freezers at 50–55 °C.
Pluxee Belgium: Malicious activity on a server. Names, emails and phone numbers possibly accessed. Payments unaffected.
The city council of La Laguna (Tenerife): its online services and file system were hit; the attackers demand $5 million and the council refuses to pay.
the banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, parent of the Belgian Keytrade Bank, reported a loss of more than €100 million through a cyberattack. No financial consequences for customers are reported.
Ryanair Pescara–Charleroi: Part of a Europe-wide hoax bomb-threat wave (27+ flights). Not attributed.
Two medical centres in Chur confirmed that patient data, including prescriptions and X-rays, and staff data were taken; the Cloak group claims 87 GB.
shipping company Maersk confirmed a breach of an older system taken over in an acquisition; a ransomware group demands $5 million.
a telecom provider (CSC Telecom) left a database of more than 125 million text messages exposed, including bank notifications and login codes for customers of Swedbank, SEB and airBaltic.
